dedupe_keys.name: unhrd stock task force stock ceilings for 44 core relief items across the humanitarian response depot network 2025

description: This case study describes how the UN Humanitarian Response Depot network, run by the World Food Programme, decided how much of each relief item to keep in stock at its hubs. The UNHRD Stock Task Force analysed the network's own dispatch records for the first 90 days of emergency responses between 2017 and 2024 and agreed a core list of 44 items, including shelter materials, water and sanitation supplies, medical items and protective equipment. Ceilings were set in two ways: a fixed number of target beneficiaries for 12 core items, and the highest demand ever recorded for the rest. Together they let the network support up to 250,000 people across all hubs in the first phase of a crisis, with 1 to 5 percent of capacity kept as a buffer; items already at their ceiling wait for the next replenishment cycle. The question-and-answer page from the June 2025 briefing is free to read on the UNHRD website; the item list and ceiling figures themselves are not available as a download. Coverage is the global UNHRD network. Caveats: a short programme description, not an evaluation; no licence is stated. Simulation uses: stock levels, lead-time assumptions and demand rules for humanitarian logistics and prepositioning models. Related records: the Global Food Twin (platform-global-food-twin) models commercial food flows that relief stocks supplement.
